units.source_text: 罢了罢了，我总想有一天教你看看我的真心，但恐我的寿命不长！

en.t: Enough, enough. I have always hoped that someday I could show you my true heart, but I fear my life will not be long.

units.source_text: 我常想不做无聊之事，以免受人怨恨，为来为去只为了你一人啊！”

en.t: I have always tried not to do foolish things, so as not to earn people's resentment; in the end, everything has been for you alone!

units.source_text: 说着，取过筝来，调整弦线，弹奏一曲。

en.t: As he spoke, he took up the zheng, tuned the strings, and played a piece.

units.source_text: 弹毕，捧过筝去，劝紫姬也弹一曲。

en.t: When he had finished playing, he offered the zheng to Lady Murasaki and urged her to play a piece as well.

units.source_text: 紫姬碰也不碰，想是听说明石姬长于弹筝，因而妒恨吧。

en.t: Lady Murasaki would not even touch it, perhaps because she had heard that Lady Akashi excelled at playing the zheng and felt jealous.

units.source_text: 紫姬原是一个温柔敦厚的美人，但看到源氏公子放荡不羁时，也不免愤怒怨恨。

en.t: Lady Murasaki was by nature a gentle, warmhearted beauty, but when she saw Prince Genji behaving so freely and recklessly, she could not help feeling anger and resentment.

units.source_text: 这倒反而使她的神情越发娇艳。

en.t: This, however, only made her expression seem all the more charming and radiant.

units.source_text: 源氏公子觉得紫姬生气时非常可爱，最宜欣赏。

en.t: Prince Genji thought Lady Murasaki was especially lovely when she was angry, and most delightful to gaze upon.
